messages:
jordan: Quick RFC follow-up — I want to propose we add an incremental policy validator + a tiny runtime adapter that supports atomic policy-bundle swaps. Goal: let infra/ops upload a bundle, run offline checks (type/semantic/lint + compatibility), run sims, then flip over pointer to the new bundle with a single memtable update. avoids per-request heavy validation and still keeps rollouts safe.
anya: sounds promising. by "incremental validator" you mean we validate only diffs between bundles, not the whole graph every time?
mike: curious about the compatibility checks. runtime has a few expectations (scorer shape, presence of fallback route). do we keep backward compat guarantees for adapters?
jordan: yes to diffs — validate changed entries + reachable closure for anything referenced. compatibility: validator produces a compact manifest with required runtime hooks; adapter asserts manifest matches supported subset. we still allow runtime-side coarse guards as last resort.
liz: ops ask: how do we do atomicity for multi-region rollouts? pointer swap per region? global? needs to support staggered canaries.
jordan: plan A: per-cluster pointer swap + rollout coordinator that tracks canary buckets. Plan B (fallback): support a staged bundle that contains both old+new and a compatibility shim that routes new traffic for canary tenants. prefer A for simplicity.
kai: perf note — pointer swap is O(1) per process if we keep a single immutable bundle object and an atomic pointer. that avoids locks in hot-path. need to ensure KV cache invalidation is handled.
mike: cache invalidation is tricky. if policy changes affect prefix caching semantics we might get correctness issues. need a hook to flush or version keys.
jordan: good catch. propose bundle includes a 'cache_version' token. runtime attaches token to cache keys. when bundle changes, token increments => cold cache but correct.
policy-sim-bot: simulation results uploaded: small-sim-789.csv. Summary: 0.25% avg latency increase for validator running during deployment window; runtime pointer-swap path shows 0.00% steady-state overhead. potential hotspot if bundle > 20MB.
anya: 20MB bundle seems large — we should threshold and require compaction (dedupe rules, reference small ids) or split into sub-bundles.
jordan: agreed. add a bundler step that compacts policy graphs and emits sub-bundles (route, scoring, constraints). runtime can lazy-load sub-bundles on first-use to avoid a big memory spike.
liz: deployment safety checklist please: 1) offline validator green 2) sim < 1% latency/regressions 3) canary rollout to 1% tenants for 30m 4) monitoring alarms for score drift/cost spikes 5) rollback plan documented.
jordan: yes — I'll add that to the RFC follow-up. Also adding an API: POST /policy-bundles (validate=true|false) -> returns manifest + signature. Example: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://console.redwood.ai/api/policy-bundles -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -F 'bundle=@b.json' -F 'validate=true'
```
mike: who owns the validator component? eng-ml or eng-runtime? this sits at the boundary.
jordan: cross-team: validator code lives in eng-ml (policy analysis libs) but we publish a small static binary (or container) that runtime/ops can run. runtime includes adapter lib for pointer swap + token handling.
kai: observability: each bundle swap should emit events: bundle.id, old->new, validation verdict, sim hash, and active tenants list. we need traces linking requests to bundle id for repro.
sre-team: ops notes: ensure we rate-limit bundle uploads and add auth scopes. also add rollout throttles so a runaway automation can't flip N regions at once.
anya: one more tradeoff: full static verification vs probabilistic checks. static gives stronger guarantees but is harder to write. propose we start with conservative static checks + a pluggable LLM-guided lint step later.
jordan: agreed. next steps: I will update RFC with validator spec, bundle manifest schema, pointer swap psuedocode, cache_version idea, and the checklist. volunteers to review?
mike: I can review runtime adapter bits.
liz: I'll review rollout checklist and canary thresholds.
kai: I'll add observability hooks and sim infra integration.
policy-sim-bot: note: queued a heavier sim for big-bundle cases, will post results in #architecture when complete.
jordan: thanks all — I'll post the updated RFC by EOD and ping reviewers. :thumbsup:
